questions.stem: What kind of unusual weather did Moscow experience this winter?
options: A) An abnormal winter snow storm.
B) The first warm front from Europe.

explain.定位:
Meanwhile in Moscow, snow completely disappeared from the city's streets as warm air
moved into the European part of Russia. An abnormally warm winter has brought flowers
into bloom.
与此同时在莫斯科，随着暖空气进入俄罗斯的欧洲部分，城市街道上的积雪完全消失了。一
个反常温暖的冬天已经让鲜花绽放。
explain.信号:
地名Moscow直接领出答案句。定位信号是地名：录音一说 Meanwhile in Moscow，就知
道讲莫斯科的内容开始了，紧跟其后的 An abnormally warm winter has brought
flowers into bloom 正面给出莫斯科是暖冬。听新闻时听到题干里的关键词（这里是
Moscow），它后面一两句就是答案句。
explain.替换:
An abnormally warm winter ↔ The unusual warm winter.
abnormally=unusual同义替换
snow completely disappeared from the city's streets ↔ The unusual warm winter.
雪消失印证是暖冬
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
An abnormal winter snow storm. 盗用了录音开头讲美国华盛顿州的 more than 63
centimeters of snow fell in just two days 和 The first big storm of the winter。暴雪确
实有，但发生在美国，不是题干问的 Moscow，属于把别处的天气安到莫斯科头上。
借用原文：The first big storm of the winter blanketed the Lake Tahoe area of Nevada with snow
B) 原词陷阱
The first warm front from Europe. 借了录音里 warm air moved into the European
part of Russia 中的 European/warm 等词凑出'来自欧洲的暖锋'。但录音说的是暖空气进
入俄罗斯的欧洲部分，并没有说'来自欧洲的第一道暖锋'，是把原词重新拼接出的假说法。
借用原文：as warm air moved into the European part of Russia
C) 张冠李戴
The frequent choking smog. 对应录音 hazardous smoke choked Beijing on Friday，
雾霾说的是北京，不是莫斯科；而且录音说的是 on Friday 这一次，并没有 frequent（频
繁）之意，既张冠李戴又夸大了频次。
借用原文：hazardous smoke choked Beijing on Friday

questions.stem: When will Beijing's air pollution index begin to decrease?

explain.定位:
Weather forecasts say the pollution should ease from Saturday afternoon when as hoped a
cold front in Beijing will disperse the smog.
天气预报说，污染应该会从周六下午开始缓解，届时如人们所愿，北京的一股冷锋将吹散
雾霾。
explain.信号:
ease+时间状语给出落点。信号是表示'减弱'的动词配时间状语：录音说 the pollution
should ease from Saturday afternoon，ease（缓解）正对应题干的 decrease（下
降），紧跟的 from Saturday afternoon 就是要找的时间。问 when 的题，就盯住事件后
面那个时间状语。
explain.替换:
from Saturday afternoon ↔ From Saturday afternoon.
时间原样对应
the pollution should ease ↔ From Saturday afternoon.
ease=decrease同义
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
From this Friday. 盗用了录音 hazardous smoke choked Beijing on Friday 里的
Friday。但周五是雾霾'袭来'的时间，不是污染'开始缓解'的时间，听到 Friday 就选，正好
把发生时间错当成缓解时间。
借用原文：hazardous smoke choked Beijing on Friday
C) 原词陷阱
In the next spring. 与录音 Several types of plants that usually wake up in the spring
中的 spring 撞词。但那句讲的是莫斯科本该春天才苏醒的植物提前开花，和北京污染缓解
毫无关系，属于借另一座城市的原词设套。
借用原文：Several types of plants that usually wake up in the spring have already bloomed
D) 原词陷阱
During the Christmas holiday. 与录音 caused travel chaos for Christmas travelers 里
的 Christmas 撞词。圣诞只是整则新闻的时间背景（讲圣诞出行受阻），并不是北京污染开
始下降的时间，听到节日词就选会被背景信息带偏。
借用原文：had caused travel chaos for Christmas travelers

questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A) The project of free digital off-line resources in Nigeria.
B) The project of free video lessons in Nigeria.
C) The digital library in Ahmadu Bello University.
D) The non-profit organizations in Ahmadu Bello University.

explain.定位:
Now, a new project provides a resource for off-line viewing at no cost. A non-profit
organization called the WiderNet Project has developed the offline eGranary Digital Library.
如今，一个新项目提供了一种可免费离线浏览的资源。一个名为 WiderNet Project 的非营
利组织开发了离线的 eGranary 数字图书馆。
explain.信号:
开头点题句 + Now 引出新主角。新闻在交代完背景（很多人没网）后，用 Now, a new
project provides a resource for off-line viewing at no cost. 这个 Now 引出真正要讲的
主角——"一个免费离线资源的新项目"。新闻的点题句通常就在开头交代完背景之后这一两
句，这里正是。
explain.替换:
a new project provides a resource for off-line viewing at no cost ↔
The project of free digital off-line resources in Nigeria.
at no cost 换成 free、resource 换成 resources
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 Math and Science video lessons for high school students 只是 eGranary 众多
资源中举的一个例子，B 盗用 video lessons 这个原词，把一个小例子放大成整则新闻的主
题，犯了以偏概全。
借用原文：Math and Science video lessons for high school students
C) 原词陷阱
Ahmadu Bello University is the largest university in Nigeria 是新闻结尾举的一个使用该
资源的例子，C 盗用 digital library 与这所大学名，把"一个使用案例"误当成新闻主题；况
且数字图书馆 eGranary 不归这所大学所有，只是被它使用。
借用原文：Ahmadu Bello University uses eGranary's digital educational resources
D) 张冠李戴
录音确实提到 A non-profit organization called the WiderNet Project，但它是开发这个
项目的机构、是讲述的工具，不是新闻要谈的中心；且原文只有一个非营利组织，D 用复数
non-profit organizations 并把它和那所大学硬凑，属张冠李戴。

eGranary Digital Library

questions.stem: What kind of resources are updated daily at eGranary?

Users can access informative websites that eGranary updates every day such as Wikipedia,
Khan Academy, Project Gutenberg, MIT OpenCourseWare, and MIT BLOSSOMS.
用户可以访问 eGranary 每天更新的信息类网站，例如维基百科、可汗学院、古登堡计划、
麻省理工开放课程以及 MIT BLOSSOMS。
explain.信号:
限定词 every day 紧贴的那类资源。题干的 daily 对应原文 eGranary updates every
day，而 every day 这个限定语紧紧挂在 informative websites 上——是"网站"被每天更
新，不是别的资源。限定词贴着谁，答案就是谁。
explain.替换:
informative websites that eGranary updates every day ↔ Informative websites
几乎原词对应，靠限定语锁定
explain.排除:

件。
借用原文：millions of digital documents, multimedia work and websites
B) 原词陷阱
digital documents 在录音里被念到（讲服务器上存了什么），B 直接搬这个原词；但它同
样没有"每天更新"的限定，是描述"存了哪些"而非"每天更新哪类"，答非所问。
借用原文：millions of digital documents
D) 原词陷阱
computer software 出现在结尾"其他资源还包括……"的清单中，D 盗用该原词；但那份清
单讲的是"还有哪些资源"，与"每天更新"无关，条件不符。

software, and educational games

questions.stem: What happened to Google's self-driving car?
options: C) It hit a driving bus in the road.
D) It hit a Lexus SUV.

explain.定位:
According to WIRED, a technology publication, the car changed traffic lanes and moved into
the path of a bus.
据科技刊物《连线》报道，这辆车变更了车道，驶入了一辆公交车的行进路线。
explain.信号:
事件主干句。这句 the car changed traffic lanes and moved into the path of a bus 是
新闻交代事故经过的主干句，紧跟在新闻开头“出了事故”之后，按新闻顺听的次序，第一道
题的答案就落在这里——它点明撞击对象是 bus。
explain.替换:
moved into the path of a bus ↔ hit a driving bus in the road
驶入公交路线即撞上行驶的公交
explain.排除:
A) 答非所问
It hit another car. 把撞击对象说成 another car（另一辆车），但录音明说撞的是 the
bus，公交不是泛指的 car，撞击对象答错。
B) 未提及
It was overspeed. 说车超速，但录音里这辆 Google 车 was moving at around 3
kilometers per hour，时速才 3 公里，根本谈不上超速，录音从没说它超速。
D) 张冠李戴
It hit a Lexus SUV. 盗用了录音原词 The driverless car was a Lexus SUV，但 Lexus SUV
说的是“这辆 Google 车本身就是雷克萨斯 SUV”，不是它撞的对象，把“它是什么车”偷换成
了“它撞了什么车”。
借用原文：The driverless car was a Lexus SUV

questions.stem: How fast was the bus when the accident happened?

explain.定位:
The speed of the bus was 24 kilometers per hour at the time of the collision.
碰撞发生时，公交车的速度是每小时 24 公里。
explain.信号:
数字配对象的精确句。这句 The speed of the bus was 24 kilometers per hour 直接把数
字和对象 bus 绑在一起，是数字题的答案句；它紧跟在前一句讲 Google 车速度 3 km/h
之后，录音故意连给两个速度，必须靠 the bus 这个对象词锁定 24。
explain.替换:
The speed of the bus was 24 kilometers per hour ↔ 24 kilometers per hour.
数字原值直接对应
explain.排除:
A) 张冠李戴
3 kilometers per hour. 盗用了录音真出现的数字 the Google car was moving at around
3 kilometers per hour，但 3 km/h 是 Google 车的速度，不是题目问的 bus 的速度，张
冠李戴。
借用原文：the Google car was moving at around 3 kilometers per hour
B) 未提及
6 kilometers per hour. 这个数字录音里压根没念过，是凭空设的干扰值，用来引诱没听清
数字、想随手蒙一个的考生。
D) 偷换概念
180 kilometers per hour. 这个偏大的数字录音并未作为速度出现，录音里近似的大数是

questions.stem: What is inevitable to self-driving cars according to Google's report?
options: A) Realities of speed and distance.
D) Driving buses in the road.

explain.定位:
We'll inevitably be involved in accidents; sometimes it's impossible to overcome the realities
of speed and distance.
我们将不可避免地卷入事故；有时候，速度与距离的现实是无法克服的。
explain.信号:
inevitably 引出的报告原话。这句出自 Google said 引用的报告原文，里面 We'll
inevitably be involved in accidents 的 inevitably 正对题干 inevitable，是“不可避免”的
直接信号；引述句 + inevitably 双重信号锁定答案句。
explain.替换:
We'll inevitably be involved in accidents ↔ Accidents in the road.
难免卷入事故即事故难免
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
Realities of speed and distance. 逐字盗用录音 the realities of speed and distance，但
这处原文搭的是 impossible to overcome（无法克服），说的是“难以克服的”，不是题干
问的“inevitable（不可避免的）”；这两个词在同句不同分句里，选项偷换了对应关系。
借用原文：it's impossible to overcome the realities of speed and distance
C) 答非所问
Wheel and fender damage. 盗用录音 The left front wheel and fender of the Google
car were damaged，但车轮和挡泥板损坏只是这一次事故的具体后果，报告说的“不可避
免”指的是 accidents，不是某个损坏部位。
借用原文：The left front wheel and fender of the Google car were damaged
D) 原词陷阱
Driving buses in the road. 借用了录音里的 bus 话题（moved into the path of a
bus），但这是描述事故怎么发生的经过，且 driving buses 表意含糊，不是报告所说“不可
避免的”那个东西。
借用原文：moved into the path of a bus

来解释自己为何找上门，这正是得知途径的落点；对话题的答案就藏在被问者应答里。

options: A) She finished her secondary school.
B) She studied in a vocational college.
C) She graduated from an open university.

男：那你上过大学吗？女：没有，我 18 岁就结束了全日制教育。

随后被问是否上过大学时，她以 No, I left full-time education when I was 18 否定大学经

I went to a secondary school in South town ↔ She finished her secondary school.

B) 与原文相反

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's occupation?
options: A) She teaches an evening class.
B) She works as a tour guide.

policewoman 出现在 I thought I'd like to be a policewoman but they turned me

explain.信号:
被问者的直接应答。女方刚问完"当了多久酒馆老板"，男方紧接着的这句应答就是答案句。
注意他说了两个数字：four years 是"当这家老板"的时长，off and on for ten years 才

explain.替换:
off and on for ten years ↔ off and on for ten years
原句几乎照搬
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱

借用原文：four years
C) 未提及
C 说酒馆"扩大他的客户网络"，但全段男方只讲了时间和酒馆类型，从没提 customer

questions.stem: What characterizes the old fashion pub according to the man?

现在我开的是大家说的那种正宗老式酒馆。就是一间带着各种社交游戏的公共酒吧，这正是

对所提事物的直接定义。男方一说出 a good old-fashioned pub，紧跟着用 That is… 给

式酒馆特征的直接说明，这句即答案句。

all the social games going with it ↔ Social games.
原话提取关键词
explain.排除:

questions.stem: What does the man say is most important in making a good pub?

Well, I think having the right customers to start with, selling the right beer, keeping it good,

questions.stem: What does the woman think of running a country pub?

转折 But 后才是真意。女方先转述"大家都觉得这是美差"，随即用 But it seems to me

借用原文：retire

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about drug abuse?
options: A) It helps the user to escape reality.
B) It is becoming increasingly popular.
C) It hurts a person and those around them.
D) It gives rise to serious social instability.

explain.定位:
Drug abuse is the use of a drug legal or illegal that hurts a person or someone close to him.
药物滥用是指使用某种药物——无论合法还是非法——以致伤害本人或与他亲近的人。
explain.信号:
定义句 is the use of。这句用 Drug abuse is the use of a drug 这种“X is …”的下定义句
式正面界定 drug abuse，是典型的定义信号；篇章独白里给主题词下定义的那一句，往往
就是出题点。
explain.替换:
hurts a person or someone close to him ↔ hurts a person and those around them
近义改写 close to him=around them
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
A 说 It helps the user to escape reality.，但定义句只讲滥用会“伤害本人及亲近者”，全篇
没有“帮人逃避现实”的表述，属于无中生有。
B) 答非所问

谁，没有说它越来越流行；这是答非所问——录音根本没在谈流行程度。
D) 过度推断
D 说 It gives rise to serious social instability.，而定义句的伤害对象只到 a person or
someone close to him（个人及亲近者）这一层，D 擅自拔高到“严重社会动荡”，属于过
度推断。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about recreational drug users?
options: A) They take drugs to get high.
B) They use drugs just for fun.
C) They use drugs as medicine.
D) They keep drug use a secret.

Recreational users take drugs to get high. They use drugs with friends or at parties to get into
the mood of things.
娱乐型使用者吸毒是为了寻求快感。他们和朋友一起或在聚会上吸毒，以融入气氛。
explain.信号:
专名后紧跟的描述句。录音点出 Recreational users take drugs to get high，专有名称
Recreational users 一出现，它后面 take drugs to get high 就是对这类人的直接界定，这
种“专名 + 紧跟描述”就是定位信号。

take drugs to get high ↔ take drugs to get high

这个限定词也把范围缩窄了，属偷换概念。

氛，没有“当药用”；全篇也没有哪类人是把毒品当药的表述，属未提及。
D) 张冠李戴

often hard to see（早期难被察觉），但那是讲“一般情况下吸毒难发现”，并非说

借用原文：In the early stages, drug use is often hard to see

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about drug dependence?
options: A) It is fatal to the user.
B) It is hard to get rid of.

Sometimes people like drugs or need drugs so much that they can't do without them. By this

有时人们如此喜欢或需要毒品，以至于离不开它。到这地步就太晚了，这个人已经“上
瘾”了。

强调句 so…that 与 too late。这里用 so much that they can't do without them（如此
以致离不开）这种 so…that 强调结构，又收以 it's too late and the person is hooked，
强烈语气标出“依赖=戒不掉”，是典型的答案信号。

can't do without them ↔ hard to get rid of

命；fatal 是把“难戒”拔成“要命”的过度推断。

questions.stem: What did Charles Harper think of while he was in hospital?

healthy frozen foods 就是“他想到了什么”的直接交代，这是答案句信号。

imagined the line of healthy frozen foods—the tasty good ↔ Producing tasty healthy frozen food

珀在医院想到的是做健康食品，不是寻找治心脏病的新方法，属偷换概念。

料调性制造“独特配料”联想，但原文说的是包装颜色暗示了新鲜与维生素，并未说配料独
特、更没说它促成成功，属未提及。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the death penalty in the United States?
options: A) It will be abolished sooner or later.
B) It is practiced in most of the states.
C) It has to be approved by the Supreme Court.
D) It has drawn a lot of criticism from overseas.

explain.定位:
In the United States, 36 states currently allow capital punishment for serious crimes such

在美国，目前有 36 个州对谋杀等严重罪行允许使用死刑。

开篇正面陈述现状的句子。这段是篇章独白，开篇第一句往往直接铺陈背景事实。36 states

36 states currently allow capital punishment ↔ It is practiced in most of the states.

other countries of the world, there is no capital punishment for minors 提到别国「没

questions.stem: What is the focus of the debate around the death penalty?
options: A) What effect it might have on youngsters.

Should there be a minimum age limit for executing criminals? ↔
Whether there should be a minimum age limit for execution.

This dream came true for me one afternoon in the ninth grade. Of course, I had heard that genius could show itself at an early age, so I was only slightly taken aback that I had achieved perfection at the tender age of 14. Obviously, I did what any professional writer would do; I hurried off to spread the good news. I didn't get very far. The first person I told was my mother.

I am not sure if she was more upset by my hubris(得意忘形) or by the fact that my English teacher had let my ego get so out of hand. In any event, my mother and her red pen showed me how deeply flawed a flawless essay could be. At the time, I am sure she thought she was teaching me about mechanics, transitions(过渡), structure, style and voice. The intimate nature of genuine criticism implies something about who is able to give it, namely, someone who knows you well enough to show you how your mental life is getting in the way of good writing. Conveniently, they are also the people who care enough to see you through this painful realization. For me it took the form of my first, and I hope only, encounter with writer's block—I was not able to produce anything for three years.

I was lucky enough to find a critic and teacher who was willing to make the journey of writing with me. E) Criticism, at its best, is deeply personal, and gets to the heart of why we write the way we do. Genuine criticism creates a precious opening for an author to become better on his own terms—a process that is often extremely painful, but also almost always meaningful.

H) My mother said she would help me with my writing, but first I had to help myself. For each assignment, I was to write the best essay I could. We do our absolute best with a piece of writing, and come as close as we can to the ideal. And, for the time being, we settle. questions.stem: What do we learn about Silicon Valley from the passage?
options: A) Its success is hard to copy anywhere else.
B) It is the biggest technology hub in the US.
C) Its fame in high technology is incomparable.
D) It leads the world in information technology.
questions.passage:
Could you reproduce Silicon Valley elsewhere, or is there something unique about it?

It wouldn't be surprising if it were hard to reproduce in other countries, because you couldn't reproduce it in most of the US either. What does it take to make a Silicon Valley?

It's the right people. If you could get the right ten thousand people to move from Silicon Valley to Buffalo, Buffalo would become Silicon Valley.

You only need two kinds of people to create a technology hub(中心): rich people and nerds(痴迷科研的人).

Observation bears this out. Within the US, towns have become startup hubs if and only if they have both rich people and nerds. Few startups happen in Miami, for example, because although it's full of rich people, it has few nerds. It's not the kind of place nerds like.

questions.stem: What happens when you have like-minded people around you all the while?
options: A) It will help your company expand more rapidly.
B) It will create a harmonious working atmosphere.
C) It may prevent your business and career from advancing.
D) It may make you feel uncertain about your own decisions.
questions.passage:
It's nice to have people of like mind around. Agreeable people boost your confidence and allow you to relax and feel comfortable. Unfortunately, that comfort can hinder the very learning that can expand your company and your career.

It's nice to have people agree, but you need conflicting perspectives to dig out the truth. If everyone around you has similar views, your work will suffer from confirmation bias(偏颇).

Take a look at your own network. Do your contacts share your point of view on most subjects? If yes, it's time to shake things up. As a leader, it can be challenging to create an environment in which people will freely disagree and argue, but as the saying goes: From confrontation comes brilliance.

It's not easy for most people to actively seek conflict. Many spend their lives trying to avoid arguments. There's no need to go out and find people you hate, but you need to do some self-assessment to determine where you have become stale in your thinking. You may need to start by encouraging your current network to help you identify your blind spots.

Passionate, energetic debate does not require anger and hard feelings to be effective. But it does require moral strength. Once you have worthy opponents, set some ground rules so everyone understands responsibilities and boundaries. The objective of this debating game is not to win but to get to the truth that will allow you to move faster, farther, and better.

writing.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay commenting on the saying “Learning is a daily experience and a lifetime mission.” You can cite examples to illustrate the importance of lifelong learning. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
writing.model:
The saying “Learning is a daily experience and a lifetime mission” reveals two truths: knowledge is built up
little by little in ordinary days, yet its pursuit never ends throughout our lives. In my view, only by treating
learning as a lifelong journey can we stay competent in a changing world.
A vivid example is my uncle, a factory worker who lost his job when machines replaced manual labour. Instead
of giving up, he studied programming every evening, and two years later he became a software tester. His story
shows that those who keep learning can keep pace with the times, while those who stop are left behind. In an
age when technology updates almost daily, continuous learning is no longer a choice but a necessity.
Therefore, we should never regard graduation as the end of study. Learning, as the saying goes, is both a daily
habit and a mission that lasts a lifetime. Only by embracing it every single day can we broaden our horizons
and enrich our lives.
